Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2476; to be non-stationary, i.e. (figuratively) homeless:--have no certain dwelling-place.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says the apostles hunger and thirst and are buffeted and have no certain dwelling place, and this is the word for that homelessness. It means to have nowhere to settle.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the apostles' wandering was not a failure of God's care, it was the shape of their calling, and Christ Himself had nowhere to lay His head.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
